headline: 242 not out: Tawhid Hridoy sets new record as highest Test scorer for Bangladesh
summary: Hridoy's historic double century against West Indies in Sylhet turns the tide, surpassing Mushfiqur Rahim's previous record.

caption:
A historic 242 not out! Tawhid Hridoy just became the highest individual run-scorer in Bangladesh's Test history.

Bangladesh batter Tawhid Hridoy struck a sensational unbeaten 242 against West Indies in the second Test in Sylhet, rewriting the country's Test cricket history.

Coming to the crease with Bangladesh at 88 for 3, Hridoy rescued the hosts from a precarious position, turning a score of 184 for 7 into a memorable first-innings lead of 30 runs.

Hridoy surpassed Mushfiqur Rahim's previous record of 219 not out to become Bangladesh's highest individual run-scorer in Test cricket.

His marathon innings, featuring 11 sixes, was brilliantly supported by Taijul Islam (22) and { "text": "Taskin Ahmed (12), as Bangladesh finished on 386 for 9." }

He became the first Bangladeshi batter to convert his maiden Test century into a double hundred and the first to score a Test double hundred against the West Indies.

Additionally, Hridoy became the first batter to score a Test double century at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium and the first Bangladeshi double-centurion in the World Test Championship.

He also set the record for the highest maiden-century score by a Bangladeshi and shared a record eighth-wicket partnership of 117 runs with Taijul Islam.

The innings ended with Shadman Islam unable to bat due to injury, leaving Bangladesh with nine wickets down.

headline_marked: [[Medical, dental exams]] likely Dec 18, barring HSC retake students
headline: Medical, dental exams likely Dec 18, barring HSC retake students
summary: Students who failed one or two subjects in HSC exams will have results by Dec 31, but medical college admissions begin mid-November, potentially excluding them.
details: The medical and dental admission tests for the 2026-27 academic session are likely to be held on December 18. This date poses a significant challenge for students who need to retake one or two subjects in their Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) exams, as their results may not be available in time for the admission process.

Students failing one or two subjects in the HSC exams can retake them from December 1, with results expected by December 31. However, the admission process for medical and dental colleges typically starts around mid-November, creating a conflict where students awaiting revised results may not meet the eligibility criteria.

Officials indicate that it is almost certain that HSC students retaking exams will not get the opportunity to sit for the medical or dental admission tests. A total of 4.23 lakh students failed one or two subjects in this year’s HSC and equivalent examinations.

The government had announced an initiative for students to retake exams in one or two subjects, aiming to prevent them from waiting another year to pass HSC. The Education Minister had stated that the ministry would try to coordinate these exams with university admissions.

Despite discussions, the December 18 date for medical and dental admission tests appears to be finalized. A notice is expected within days, with a meeting at the health ministry to discuss seat numbers also scheduled.

Two new government medical colleges in Thakurgaon and Narsingdi, each with 50 seats, are being included in the admission process for the 2026-27 academic session. This will bring the total number of public medical colleges to 40, alongside 72 private ones.
